newsitem.title: USA: Dlr rise tends to restrain import prices - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rise tends to restrain import prices - Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday said that central bank policy makers take into account exchange rates in decisions on monetary policy and noted a stronger dollar tends to restrain import prices.

"It is certainly the case that when the dollar rises relative ot other currencies, other things (being) equal, import prices tend to be less expansive," Greenspan said in response to a question during testimony before the Senate Finance Committee.

To the extent that import prices have an effect on overall inflation, policy makers on the Federal Open Market Committee take the exchange rate into account when they make interest-rate determinations, Greenspan said.
But he added it is "almost never" the determining factor for such decisions.
